newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says French economy upturn marred by jobless.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says French economy upturn marred by jobless.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Friday the French economy was reviving but that an expanding workforce was keeping unemployment stubbornly high.

"It's true that the French economy is rebounding well and that indicators are tending to show green, that corporate order books are picking up again," Juppe said at an job training exhibition in the southwestern city of Bordeaux.
But he said that the "big difficulty over unemployment is that the active population is continuing to rise for businesses -- 160,000 more in 1997."

"That is what's making things difficult, because even when the economy works better, starts creating jobs again, we have some trouble being sufficiently creative to absorb this new population," he said. "We have to act on all fronts."

The centre-right government expects economic growth to accelerate to at least 2.3 percent in 1997 from 1.3 percent in 1996 and hopes this will help cut record unemployment of 12.7 percent of the workforce.
"We're working all this out and I'm confident that the second half of 1997 should allow us to reverse the trend in the right direction," said Juppe, who is also mayor of Bordeaux.
Most private economists say growth will not be strong enough to solve the unemployment problem and do not expect the jobless rate to fall significantly before the end of 1998.
The government also hopes that a revival of growth will simplify its task in qualifying for a single European currency from 1999.
Juppe said "many things have been achieved" since his conservative ally President Jacques Chirac took office promising a war on jobs.
Juppe has often expressed optimism about the outlook, in contrast to gloom among French people. A year ago, he declared "springtime for France".
